{{alias}}( ID, N, D )
    Sorts an array of doubles in increasing or decreasing order using
    quicksort, with insertion sort for small partitions (size <= 20).

    Indexing is relative to the first index. To introduce an offset,
    use typed array views.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ID: string
        Sort direction: 'Increasing' or 'Decreasing'.

    N: NonNegativeInteger
        Number of elements to sort.

    D: Float64Array
        Array to sort in-place.

    Returns
    -------
    out: integer
        Status code. If success, the function returns `0`; otherwise,
        the function returns `-i`, where `i` is the index of the
        argument having an invalid value.

    Examples
    --------
    > var D = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 5, 7, 9, 3, 11 ] );
    > {{alias}}( 'Increasing', 5, D );
    > D
    <Float64Array>[ 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 ]

    // Using typed array views:
    > var D0 = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 0, 5, 7, 9, 3, 11 ] );
    > D = new Float64Array( D0.buffer, D0.BYTES_PER_ELEMENT*1 );
    > {{alias}}( 'Increasing', 5, D );
    > D0
    <Float64Array>[ 0, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 ]


{{alias}}.ndarray( ID, N, D, strideD, offsetD )
    Sorts an array of doubles in increasing or decreasing order using
    quicksort, with insertion sort for small partitions (size <= 20)
    using alternative indexing semantics.

    While typed array views mandate a view offset based on the underlying
    buffer, the offset parameter supports indexing semantics based on
    a starting index.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ID: string
        Sort direction: 'Increasing' or 'Decreasing'.

    N: NonNegativeInteger
        Number of elements to sort.

    D: Float64Array
        Array to sort in-place.

    strideD: integer
        Stride length for `D`.

    offsetD: integer
        Starting index for `D`.

    Returns
    -------
    out: integer
        Status code. If success, the function returns `0`; otherwise,
        the function returns `-i`, where `i` is the index of the
        argument having an invalid value.

    Examples
    --------
    > var D = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 5, 7, 9, 3, 11 ] );
    > {{alias}}.ndarray( 'Increasing', 5, D, 1, 0 );
    > D
    <Float64Array>[ 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 ]

    // Using typed array views:
    > var D0 = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 0, 5, 7, 9, 3, 11 ] );
    > D = new Float64Array( D0.buffer, D0.BYTES_PER_ELEMENT*1 );
    > {{alias}}.ndarray( 'Increasing', 5, D, 1, 0 );
    > D0
    <Float64Array>[ 0, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 ]

    See Also
    --------
